PullRequest.Title: sessions: balance chat and detail tab spacing
PullRequest.Body:

Balance label and Close-button spacing in Agents-window chat tabs, and keep detail-pane icon insets consistent without changing ordinary editor-tab geometry.

Follow-up to #340635. Fixes #336471. Related to #331234 and #339782; these broader spacing reports are non-closing references.

## Changes

- Separate standalone chat-tab padding from editor file-icon gutters. Use logical toolbar spacing and a compact trailing inset only when a chat has tab actions.
- Give docked detail tabs their own leading icon inset, preserving the RTL file-icon gutter and excluding modal editors.
- Preserve Connected RTL shoulders and aligned terminal outlines without an opaque cap covering labels. For an actually right-clipped tab, retain a stroke-only viewport boundary; distinguish real clipping from rounded `clientWidth` at fractional widths.
- Use a border-based strip separator and cover RTL scrolling, terminal closing, tab rebuilding, and clipping-state disposal.

## Testing

1. Enable Modern UI with Connected tabs. Open a main chat and related chats; compare their label and Close-button spacing in LTR and RTL.
2. With running chats, hover an inactive tab and its Close button, then switch the active chat. Check readable labels, compact trailing spacing, and unobstructed actions. Repeat with Pill tabs.
3. Overflow the Connected strip in RTL. Partially clip an active nonterminal tab at either viewport edge, then reveal and close the terminal chat. Check the visible outline, replacement shoulder, scroll clamping, and removal of stale clipping paint in regular and high-contrast themes.
4. Check aligned RTL tabs at fractional widths and zoom levels: alignment must not create an extra viewport stroke. Verify the docked Changes tab with file icons enabled and disabled.
5. Compare ordinary editor tabs, including compact, sticky, action-reservation, and high-contrast states, with the behavior from #340635.

Local validation:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatCompositeBar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Changed-file ESLint and Stylelint — passed.
- Headless component renders preserve exact same-platform editor image bytes against the clean base and chat/detail image bytes against the approved reference. Direct raster checks verify the visible high-contrast RTL viewport stroke.
- Independent local code review and read-only Copilot CLI review completed; the RTL truncation finding is addressed.

## Visual comparison

Matched dark-theme, running-chat scenes at the same viewport, zoom, and device scale; spinner animation is frozen. An inactive Close button is hovered.

Before:

![Before: inactive Close hover with the wider trailing inset](./baseline-running-tabs-inactive-close-hover.png)

After:

![After: inactive Close hover with the compact trailing inset](./candidate-running-tabs-inactive-close-hover.png)

Corner-contour refinement and wrapped editor-action overlap are separate workstreams; this PR does not claim to resolve them.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll an overflowing Connected chat-tab strip, including RTL and fractional-width clipping
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A native or custom scrollbar event synchronously calls ChatCompositeBar._updateConnectedTabClipping before the scroll presentation is complete. The method clears prior clipping classes, reads the active tab and viewport geometry, updates clipping classes, and now toggles one additional truncation class from already-read bounds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous DOM geometry/style reads via getBoundingClientRect, clientWidth, and getComputedStyle during scroll
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(1) per delivered scroll callback: three bounding-rectangle reads, one clientWidth read, and one computed-style read for the single active tab; independent of total tab count except for the pre-existing linear active-tab lookup
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same geometry and computed-style reads, class clearing, and clipping class writes already ran on each callback. The diff adds an O(1) comparison using cached rectangles and one class toggle, without adding a geometry read or scaling the work by tab count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on the scroll path and can participate in layout/style resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll event frequency; only the single active tab is measured and updated. The added work remains O(1) for any number of chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the UI thread, following the existing native-scroll and ScrollableElement callbacks; no new queue, parallelism, or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. The new truncation state is recomputed from the same current geometry used by the existing clipping calculation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and O(1) added work from the changed method and its two existing scroll listeners.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser class invalidation cost varies, but the new class affects one overflow-edge element and does not introduce an additional forced geometry/style read; no realistic material regression is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not add a new layout boundary or increase geometry-read cardinality; it adds only a bounded state toggle needed to distinguish physical truncation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, rebuild, activate, and dispose chat tabs with close actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat-list changes rebuild each tab and active-chat changes update/reveal the active tab. The diff adds one class to each already-created non-main tab and clears the new clipping class during existing clipping cleanup and disposal.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats in one group. The added class assignment is O(1) per non-main tab during an already O(n) rebuild; cleanup is O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread DOM construction and disposal; no async fan-out, limiter, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is introduced or moved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or retained map is added. The marker resides on the tab DOM node and is released with the existing tab/container lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from _rebuildTabs, _createTab, _clearConnectedTabClipping, and dispose ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Toolbar construction cost can scale with chats, but that construction predates the diff; the new marker itself is negligible and bounded by live tabs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change neither retains additional long-lived objects nor introduces heavyweight per-tab work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render ordinary editor tabs and docked detail-pane tabs with adjusted icon insets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS selector matching and style calculation apply the new custom-property-based padding when tabs are rendered or restyled. No JavaScript, data fetch, or external operation blocks progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered editor tabs during normal style recalculation. The selectors replace existing padding declarations and add two detail-pane-scoped declarations; no per-tab DOM or layout loop is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style calculation on the UI thread; no explicit scheduling or concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal browser style caching only; no application cache key or invalidation behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the runtime effect is declarative spacing only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact selector-matching cost is browser-dependent, but the selectors are scoped to existing tab structures and provide no concrete mechanism for material added layout or rendering cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The CSS changes alter geometry but do not establish repeated forced layout, unbounded rendering work, or a new expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files. The only hot path touched is Connected-tab scroll clipping; its added work is constant-time and reuses existing geometry reads. Tab lifecycle and CSS spacing changes add no actionable CPU, memory, I/O, IPC, network, cache, or concurrency regression.
